meta.default_jurisdiction: UAE federal private sector (Federal Decree-Law 33/2021 as amended)
meta.source_checked: Official UAE legislation portal sources checked for Decree-Law 33/2021, Cabinet Resolution 1/2022, Cabinet Resolution 27/2024, Federal Decree-Law 13/2022, Cabinet Resolution 97/2022, and the UAE Government public-holidays page. See per-item source URLs and verification notes; residence-visa sponsorship remains out of scope.

source_status_legend.verified: Relevant article text or official government page text was retrieved and checked; see source URL and article/page reference.
source_status_legend.partially_verified: Some legal points are supported, but the question extends beyond the verified source coverage.

meta.note: Evaluation material for a software project. Not legal advice. Applies by default to UAE federal private-sector employment; confirm jurisdiction and current amendments.

items.question: Am I entitled to sick leave?
required_facts: After probation, up to 90 days of sick leave per year, continuous or intermittent
First 15 days full pay, next 30 days half pay, remainder unpaid
Must inform the employer within 3 working days and provide a medical report from a medical entity
No paid sick leave during probation; employer may grant unpaid sick leave

items.question: Is there maternity leave?
required_facts: 60 days: first 45 days full wage, next 15 days half wage
Up to 45 additional unpaid days if sickness of the mother or child resulting from pregnancy or childbirth prevents return, with a medical certificate
Termination because of pregnancy or maternity leave is not permitted

items.question: When is my salary supposed to arrive in my bank account?
required_facts: Employer must pay wages on their due dates under the Ministry's regulations and the Implementing Regulation
The law does not set one universal payday; the due date comes from the contract and payroll arrangements
Must not invent a specific date
items.notes: Article 16(1)(a)-(b) says wages are paid on contractual due dates and agreed manner, under Ministry regulations/standards; MOHRE-registered establishments use WPS or another Ministry-approved system. No universal payday is set.

items.question: Do I have unemployment compensation?
required_facts: Says unemployment compensation comes from a separate unemployment insurance scheme
Eligibility requires at least 12 consecutive months of subscription
Compensation is 60% of the subscription salary
Compensation is paid for up to 3 months per claim
A claim must be submitted within 30 days from termination
Says whether this user is covered cannot be determined without their subscription and termination details

sources.doc: Federal Decree-Law No. 13 of 2022 concerning Insurance Against Unemployment
Cabinet Resolution No. 97 of 2022 concerning the mechanisms and controls for implementing the unemployment insurance scheme

items.notes: Do not conclude the user personally qualifies without confirming subscription/payment status, involuntary loss circumstances, exclusions and the other statutory conditions. Decree-Law 13/2022 Article 5 lists core eligibility conditions; Article 6 covers value and period. Cabinet Resolution 97/2022 provides implementation details.

items.question: Is it mandatory for a company to sponsor visas?
required_facts: No one may work or be employed in the UAE without a work permit from the Ministry
The employer may not charge the worker recruitment and employment fees or costs, directly or indirectly
States that residence visa sponsorship rules are not covered by the sources it has
items.notes: Partial-coverage case: answer that a required work permit is needed and the employer cannot charge recruitment/employment costs to the worker. The sources in this dataset do not establish the precise residence-visa sponsorship obligation; abstain on that portion until applicable immigration/residence legislation and the employer regime are verified.

items.question: I have worked here for 3 full years. What is the minimum paid annual leave I am entitled to per year?
required_facts: Not less than 30 days for each year of service
items.jurisdiction_behavior: Assume UAE federal private-sector law. If the user states DIFC or ADGM, do not apply this answer; retrieve that jurisdiction’s employment law. Do not imply that every other free zone has a separate employment law.
items.notes: The article says 'thirty days' and does not say 'calendar days'. Do not require that wording.

items.question: I joined on 1 January 2026 and I resign on 31 July 2026 (7 months of service). How many annual leave days have I earned at minimum?
required_facts: Two days per month when service is more than six months and less than a year
items.notes: For this exact scenario, 1 January to 31 July is stated as seven months: 7 × 2 = 14 days. Article 29(9) concerns payment for unused accrued leave on termination. If dates are partial months or a different leave-year policy is relevant, verify the applicable calculation and contract.
items.calculation: 7 months of service × 2 days per month = 14 days. This assumes the stated dates amount to seven months of service and applies Article 29(1)(b).

items.question: My monthly basic salary is AED 15,000 and I have completed exactly 4 years of full-time service. What end-of-service gratuity am I entitled to?
items.calculation: 21 days of basic wage × 4 years = 84 days. Daily wage = AED 15,000 ÷ 30 = AED 500. Gratuity = 84 × AED 500 = AED 42,000.
required_facts: 21 days of basic wage for each of the first five years
Calculated on the basic wage only, not allowances
Requires at least one year of continuous service
items.notes: Calculation assumes four full years of continuous eligible service, full-time foreign worker under the standard gratuity regime, and no applicable alternative savings/pension scheme or adjustment. Article 51 sets 21 days’ basic wage for each of the first five years; Article 67 defines a month as 30 days. Verify current legal applicability and any unpaid-leave adjustment for an individual claim.

items.question: My contract says 60 days notice. How much notice do I have to give if I resign?
required_facts: Notice period is the one agreed in the contract
The law requires it to be between 30 and 90 days
Notice must be in writing
items.jurisdiction_behavior: Assume UAE federal private-sector law. Notice is written and follows the contract, within the statutory 30–90 day range; check a separate regime such as DIFC/ADGM if applicable.

items.question: What are the official maximum working hours?
required_facts: Normal working hours are limited to 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week, subject to statutory exceptions.
Normal working hours are reduced by two hours during Ramadan under Cabinet Resolution 1/2022 Article 15(2).
items.notes: Article 15(2) of Cabinet Resolution 1/2022 expressly provides the two-hour reduction during Ramadan. Do not present the general maximum as applying without exception to every worker/category.

items.question: Which are the public holidays for 2027?
required_facts: Lists the public holidays with their date rules and durations: New Year, Eid Al-Fitr, Arafa Day, Eid Al-Adha, Hijri New Year, Prophet's Birthday, National Day
Does not present Gregorian dates for the Islamic holidays as confirmed, and says they depend on the official announcement
Says the Cabinet may move some holidays (not the Eid holidays) to the start or end of the week

sources.doc: Cabinet Resolution No. 27 of 2024 Concerning the Public Holidays in the State
Official UAE Government portal, Public Holidays

items.notes: Use the statutory holiday list and durations from Cabinet Resolution 27/2024 Article 1. Gregorian equivalents for Islamic holidays in 2027 are estimates only and must not be represented as officially confirmed dates. If giving date estimates, state that they are calendar projections, not dates specified in the resolution.

items.question: When will the dates of the holidays be confirmed?
required_facts: Islamic holidays follow the Hijri calendar
Says the sources do not specify when dates are announced, without inventing a deadline

sources.doc: Official UAE Government portal, Public Holidays

items.notes: There is no single confirmation date for every holiday. Fixed Gregorian holidays are known from the legislation; Islamic holiday dates depend on the official moon-sighting determination and are confirmed near the occasion.

items.question: What do the holiday dates depend on?
required_facts: Gregorian holidays (New Year, National Day) are fixed dates
Islamic holidays are defined by Hijri dates
Eid Al-Fitr gets an extra day if Ramadan completes 30 days

sources.doc: Official UAE Government portal, Public Holidays

items.notes: Gregorian public holidays have fixed Gregorian dates under Cabinet Resolution 27/2024. Islamic holidays are defined by Hijri dates and depend on moon sighting. Eid Al-Fitr’s holiday includes an additional day if Ramadan completes 30 days, under Cabinet Resolution 27/2024 Article 1.

items.question: I work in a DIFC company. How many days of annual leave do I get?
required_facts: Says its v1 sources cover UAE federal private-sector law only
Does not answer with the federal number as if it applied to DIFC

items.question: How many days of annual leave do I get?
required_facts: Answers 30 days per year under UAE federal law
States the federal-law assumption and says free zones may differ
items.jurisdiction_behavior: Answer 30 days per year under UAE federal private-sector law if that jurisdiction is established. Ask/clarify jurisdiction if material; do not state that all free zones have separate employment laws. DIFC and ADGM have separate employment regimes.
